questions.question: Discuss the concept and major features of economic decoupling.
questions.solution_html:
•  Economic decoupling refers to reducing economic dependence between countries.
  •  Reduced trade and investment between countries.
  •  Diversification of supply chains.
  •  Increased domestic production - Greater economic self-reliance.

questions.question: Explain the possibility of retaliation associated with tariff policy.
questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Explain why a labour-abundant country specializes in labour-intensive goods according to the Heckscher–Ohlin Theory.
questions.solution_html:
• according to Heckscher Ohlin Theory.
  •  Labour abundance: The country has more labour relative to capital.
  •  Lower labour cost: Abundant labour makes labour relatively cheaper.
  •  Labour-intensive goods: These goods require more labour than capital.
  •  Comparative advantage: Such goods can be produced at a lower relative cost.
  •  Specialization: The country specializes in and exports labour-intensive goods.
  •  Example: India exports garments and textiles due to its large labour force.
questions.final_answer:  Example: India exports garments and textiles due to its large labour force
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Explain the major "basis of international trade"
questions.solution_html:
•  Natural resources: Differences in resource availability.
  •  Factor endowments: Differences in labour and capital.
  •  Production costs: Differences in the cost of producing goods.
  •  Comparative advantage: Lower opportunity cost of production.
  •  Technology: Differences in technological development and skills.
  •  Economies of scale: Lower average costs through large-scale production.
questions.final_answer:  Economies of scale: Lower average costs through large-scale production
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: Discuss the role of bank rate policy in correcting BOP disequilibrium.
questions.solution_html:
•  Higher bank rate: Reduces borrowing and money supply.
  •  Lower imports: Reduces spending and demand for imported goods.
  •  Foreign capital inflow: Higher interest rates may attract foreign investment.
  •  Controls inflation: May improve export competitiveness.
  •  Corrects BoP deficit: Reduces foreign exchange outflow and encourages inflow.
questions.final_answer:  Corrects BoP deficit: Reduces foreign exchange outflow and encourages inflow
questions.source_exam: V Semester MGU UGP (Honours) - 2024 Admission regular Examination October 2026

questions.question: / exchange rate is determined in the foreign exchange market.
questions.solution_html:
• exchange market.
  •  Demand for foreign exchange (D): Slopes downward.
  •  Supply of foreign exchange (S): Slopes upward.
  •  Equilibrium exchange rate: D=S
  •  Equilibrium point (E): Intersection of demand and supply curves.
  •  Above equilibrium: Excess supply of foreign exchange.
  •  Below equilibrium: Excess demand for foreign exchange.
questions.final_answer: Option (d) : Slopes downward.

  •  Demand for foreign exchange (D): Slopes downward.
  •  Supply of foreign exchange (S): Slopes upward.
  •  Equilibrium exchange rate: D=S
  •  Equilibrium point (E): Intersection of demand and supply curves.

  •  Below equilibrium: Excess demand for foreign exchange.

questions.question: Evaluate why migration should be analysed from both sending- and receiving-country perspectives.
questions.solution_html:
• perspectives.
  •  Sending countries: Migration reduces unemployment and increases remittances but may
  • cause brain drain and labour shortages.
  •  Receiving countries: Migration fills labour shortages and supports economic growth but
  • may increase pressure on public services.
questions.final_answer: may increase pressure on public services
